title: Identifying Message Chains Smell
question: Which of the following statements best describes the 'Message Chains' code smell?

options.text: A method is filled with explanatory comments because the code is not self-documenting.
In code you see a series of calls resembling $a->b()->c()->d().
Two code fragments look almost identical, leading to maintenance issues.
A class doesn't do enough to earn your attention and its responsibilities should be moved elsewhere.

explanation: A 'Message Chain' occurs when a client requests an object, that object requests another, which requests yet another, and so on (e.g., `a.getB().getC().doSomething()`). This creates a strong coupling between the client and the structure of the chain, making the code fragile to changes in intermediate relationships.
